step_by_step_reasoning:
The architecture diagram displays Tally Prime on AWS using a multi-account structure split between an Admin account and Customer Pod accounts.

1. User Authentication Flow (Admin Account):
- The user initiates authentication request via API Gateway (LOGIN API).
- LOGIN API triggers the Auth Lambda function.
- Auth Lambda sends a second-level authentication request to the external Tally.net backend server.
- Auth Lambda interacts with AWS KMS (Customer Master Key) to generate/sign the authentication token.
- Key material and signed secret tokens are returned back through Auth Lambda and API Gateway to the User.

2. User Session Execution Flow (Pod Account):
- The user connects using NICE DCV (via Web Browser or Thick Client) through Amazon CloudFront.
- Lambda@Edge (L@E) on CloudFront routes the request to the correct Application Load Balancer (ALB).
- ALB distributes traffic to target EC2 instances running Docker containers with Wine and Tally Prime inside an ECS cluster.
- Container instances re-authenticate session requests back with the Auth Lambda in the Admin Account.

edges.notes: User initiates authentication request to Login API Gateway.
Login API Gateway invokes Auth Lambda function.
Auth Lambda verifies credentials with Tally.net backend.
Auth Lambda requests key signing operations from KMS.
KMS returns cryptographic token materials to Auth Lambda.
Auth Lambda returns generated session token to Login API.
Login API returns session authentication token to User.
User connects via NICE DCV through CloudFront using authentication token.
CloudFront triggers Lambda@Edge for routing dynamic pod selection.
Lambda@Edge routes request to appropriate ALB.
ALB routes session connection to target Container running Tally Prime with Wine.
ECS cluster orchestrates and manages container lifecycle on Linux EC2.
Container re-authenticates active session back with Auth Lambda in Admin account.
